Background The VA Cheyenne Healthcare System is committed to providing the highest quality of care and service to the Veterans it serves. As part of that commitment, the facility continually evaluates the patient experience to identify opportunities for improvement. In recent years, VA Cheyenne has seen an increasing number of Patient Record Flags (PtRFs) and patient complaints related to wayfinding challenges across the campus. Specifically, Veterans and visitors have reported difficulty locating their clinics and appointments, parking in incorrect or inconvenient areas, and being required to walk excessive distances — a particular hardship for those managing chronic medical conditions, mobility limitations, or disabilities. These challenges not only create frustration and anxiety for Veterans before they even reach their point of care, but they can also result in missed or delayed appointments, increased staff burden, and a negative overall impression of the facility. For many Veterans, particularly those with physical or cognitive impairments, navigating an unfamiliar medical campus can be an overwhelming experience that detracts from the care they came to receive. VA Cheyenne Healthcare System recognizes that improving the Veteran patient experience extends beyond the clinical encounter — it begins the moment a Veteran decides to visit the campus.
